subject: math-aa-sl
topicLabel: Number & algebra — 1.1 toolkit, 1.2 sequences, 1.3 exponents & logs

items.stem: Write 0.000456 in standard form (scientific notation).
items.note: Move the decimal 4 places right → negative exponent 4. One non-zero digit before the decimal point.

items.stem: The number 2678 rounded to 3 significant figures is:
items.note: Digits 2, 6, 7 with next digit 8 ≥ 5 → round the third figure up: 267 → 268 → 2680.

items.stem: A length is measured as 34.5 cm, true value 35.0 cm. The percentage error is approximately:
items.note: |34.5−35.0|/35.0 × 100 = 0.5/35.0 × 100 ≈ 1.43% → 1.4% (2 s.f.). Percentage error is always non-negative.

items.stem: The 10th term of the arithmetic sequence 7, 12, 17, … is:
items.note: uₙ = u₁ + (n−1)d = 7 + 9 × 5 = 52. Using n instead of n−1 gives 57 — the classic off-by-one in sequences.

items.stem: The sum of the first 20 terms of the arithmetic series 3 + 7 + 11 + … is:
A geometric sequence has u₁ = 5 and r = 3. The 6th term is:
Which series is geometric with r = −½ and has sum to infinity?
items.note: r = −½ has |r| < 1 → S∞ = u₁/(1−r) = 8/1.5 = 16/3 converges. Infinite sums need |r| < 1.

items.stem: Simplify (3x²y)³ ÷ (9xy²).
items.note: (3x²y)³ = 27x⁶y³; 27/9 = 3, x⁶/x = x⁵, y³/y² = y → 3x⁵y. All three laws at once: power of a product, then divide coefficients and subtract exponents.

items.stem: 2⁵ × 2⁻² ÷ 2³ equals:
items.note: Add exponents for multiplication, subtract for division: 5−2−3 = 0 → 2⁰ = 1.

items.stem: If log₂ x = 5, then x equals:
items.note: log₂ x = 5 ⇒ x = 2⁵ = 32. Logs are exponent questions in disguise.

items.stem: log₃ 81 equals:
log 8 + log 9, written as a single logarithm (base 10), is:
items.note: Sum of logs = log of product: log(8×9) = log 72. Difference would be a quotient.

items.stem: Solve 3ˣ = 81.
items.note: 81 = 3⁴ → x = 4. For non-obvious values: x = log 81 / log 3 = 4.

items.stem: The first term of an arithmetic sequence is 12 and the 5th term is 0. The common difference is:
items.note: u₅ = 12 + 4d = 0 → d = −3. Solve linearly — no guess-and-check needed.

items.stem: ∑ (2k + 1) for k = 1 to 10 equals:
items.note: Terms: 3,5,…,21 — arithmetic with 10 terms: S = 10/2 × (3+21) = 120. Sigma notation is just a packed series.

items.stem: A population of 5000 grows by 4% per year. After 3 whole years it is closest to:
items.note: Compound growth: 5000 × 1.04³ = 5624.32. Percent growth per period is always a power, never repeated addition.

items.stem: The value of 27^(2/3) is:
items.note: Cube root first: 27^(1/3) = 3, then square: 3² = 9. Fractional exponents = root then power.

items.stem: If logₓ 16 = 2, then x =
items.note: x² = 16 → x = 4 (base must be positive and ≠ 1).

items.stem: An investment doubles every 9 years. Written as an exponential, value after t years is proportional to:
items.note: Doubling time T: multiplier 2^(t/T). Growth models appear in both Paper 2 and IA contexts.

items.stem: The exact value of (2⁻³ + 2⁻¹) × 2² is:
items.note: 2⁻³ = 1/8, 2⁻¹ = 1/2 → sum = 5/8 → ×4 = 20/8 = 5/2. Paper 1 is no-calculator: exact fractions only.

items.stem: The third term of an arithmetic sequence is 14 and the eighth term is 39. Find the first term, the common difference, and the sum of the first 15 terms.
markscheme: u₃ = a + 2d = 14 and u₈ = a + 7d = 39 (1 for setting up)
items.tactic: Two-unknown sequence problems: write two uₙ equations, solve simultaneously. Show GDC-free working — this is Paper 1 territory.

items.stem: (a) Solve 2ˣ⁺¹ = 16. (b) Hence or otherwise solve log₂(x + 3) = 4.
markscheme: (a) 2ˣ⁺¹ = 2⁴ → x + 1 = 4 → x = 3 (2: 1 for equating exponents, 1 for answer)
Clear communication of both parts with correct notation (1)
items.tactic: 'Hence' means use part (a)'s method: convert logs to exponents. Always state the domain check for log equations.
